question: What type of environment does Mycobacterium tuberculosis need to grow?
explanation: This bacterium is an obligate aerobe, meaning it requires oxygen to survive and multiply within host tissues. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why does tuberculosis treatment take many months instead of just a few days?

options.A: The immune system fights off the medicine
options.B: The patient forgets to take doses daily
options.C: The drugs used are extremely weak

explanation: Because the bacteria have a slow replication cycle, medications must be given over a long duration to catch them as they divide. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which major component makes up a large part of the cell wall of Mycobacterium tuberculosis?
explanation: The cell wall is rich in lipids and mycolic acids, which give the bacterium its protective waxy coat. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason standard Gram staining fails to work on Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.A: The cells dissolve completely in alcohol
options.B: The bacteria only stain when exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: The waxy cell wall blocks dyes from entering
options.D: The bacteria are too large to see under light

explanation: The thick layer of lipids and waxes prevents standard water-soluble stains from penetrating the bacterial cell. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h2)

question: Where in the respiratory tract do inhaled tuberculosis droplets typically settle?
explanation: The droplets are small enough to bypass the upper airway and reach the deep lung alveoli where infection is established. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the tubercle formed by the immune system?

options.A: To wall off and trap the bacteria
options.B: To help the bacteria spread faster
options.C: To pump oxygen to the infected tissue
options.D: To produce extra red blood cells

explanation: The immune system creates granulomas or tubercles to isolate the bacilli and prevent them from spreading through the body. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which symptom is considered a classic sign of pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: A persistent cough lasting over two weeks
options.B: Itchy skin rashes across the chest
options.C: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities
options.D: Painful cramping in the abdominal muscles

explanation: A chronic cough that lingers for more than two weeks is the standard screening trigger for suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h4)

question: A patient presents with fever, night sweats, weight loss, and back pain with spinal deformity. Which condition is most likely present?
explanation: Spinal tuberculosis, or Pott's disease, affects the vertebrae and can cause back pain alongside systemic tuberculosis symptoms. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the main advantage of the GeneXpert MTB/RIF molecular test over traditional sputum microscopy?

options.A: It does not require any electric power source
options.B: It detects bacterial DNA and drug resistance rapidly
options.C: It grows live bacteria within twenty minutes
options.D: It is completely free to produce in any clinic

explanation: GeneXpert provides fast molecular results and identifies rifampicin resistance without waiting weeks for cultures to grow. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why do laboratories still perform bacterial culture testing even though it takes many weeks?

options.A: It is the gold standard for definitive diagnosis and full drug testing
options.B: It gives results faster than any other available screening tool
options.C: It replaces the need for patient physical examinations entirely
options.D: It only requires a simple drop of capillary blood from a finger

explanation: Culture allows growth of the organism for comprehensive drug susceptibility testing across multiple medications. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h5)

question: How many first-line medications are typically given during the intensive phase of standard tuberculosis treatment?
explanation: The intensive phase utilizes isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol simultaneously to reduce bacterial load quickly. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary danger when a patient stops taking their tuberculosis medications halfway through the course?

options.A: The lungs will instantly regenerate healthy tissue
options.B: The diagnostic tests will always show negative results
options.C: The bacteria can develop resistance to standard drugs
options.D: The patient will immediately catch a viral cold

explanation: Incomplete treatment allows surviving bacteria to mutate and develop resistance, making future infections harder to treat. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which first-line anti-tuberculosis medication is avoided during pregnancy due to fetal toxicity?
explanation: Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside that can cross the placenta and cause hearing loss in the fetus. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h7)

question: A midwife is counseling a new mother with active tuberculosis about breastfeeding and infant care. Which practice is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop all maternal medications immediately to protect the baby
options.B: Delay infant BCG vaccination until the child reaches school age
options.C: Separate the newborn from the mother permanently on day one
options.D: Continue treatment and breastfeeding while taking appropriate precautions

explanation: Mothers on appropriate treatment can safely breastfeed, as drug concentrations in breast milk are too low to harm or treat the infant. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T7#BMP116_U2_T7_h7)
